VO in the 3-state condition is recommended from 0 to 5.5 V (6.3), and any output in the high-impedance or power-off state is rated to 7 V absolute (6.1), so it takes the 3.6 V connector level. No bus hold is stated. II is +-1 uA at VCC 0 to 5.5 V, so the pad's 113 kOhm reset pull-down holds an input at 0.11 V, under VIL 0.3 x VCC (0.96 V at 3.201 V). VIH is 0.7 x VCC, 2.38 V at 3.399 V, against the pad's 2.62 V VOH. At VCC 3.3 V +-0.3 V and CL 50 pF (6.9): tpd 13.5 ns max, tdis 18 ns max, tsk(o) 1.5 ns. Recommended IOH/IOL is -8/8 mA at 3 to 3.6 V (6.3). TA -40 to 125 C. Supply 2 to 5.5 V. It misses P2's series-resistance line as written: 3.4 V / 142 Ohm = 23.9 mA is 3 times its 8 mA. It meets V75's found value, which sizes the resistor to the element's own recommended current: at least 3.4 V / 8 mA = 425 Ohm. That resistor gives 425 Ohm x 50 pF = 21 ns. The connector then idles at about (3.201 - 0.3 mA x 65 Ohm) x 10/10.425 = 3.05 V into the 10 kOhm pull-down, where 65 Ohm is taken from the -8 mA row as P2 does. That is above EFM8BB21's 2.7 V. The re-rank should decide whether the resistor follows the element. JLCPCB (vendors.py jlcpcb C475502, 2026-09-29T05:05:40Z): stockCount 12478, canPresaleNumber 12437, expand, USD 0.2453 at 1. The need is 2 a board x 5 = 10, so the gate is 50: pass. exclusions_not_holding.part: SN74LV4T125PWR (C90755), Texas Instruments, dropped under gated output buffer
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: fails load and series resistance: every switching figure at CL 15 or 30 pF, none at 50 pF (SCLS749C 6.6); IOH -8 mA and IOL 8 mA at VCC 3.3 V (6.3), so a short through 142 Ohm draws 23.9 mA, three times the recommended output current
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The series-resistance ground does not hold. V75's found value sets each line's lower bound from the recommended output current of the element that drives it: 275 Ohm for the pad and 142 Ohm for 'a line driven by a 244' at 24 mA. The resistor is a round-2 part. For an 8 mA element the bound is 3.4 V / 8 mA = 425 Ohm, which meets V75. The 142 Ohm is the 244's figure, not a limit on other parts. The load ground stands. SCLS749C (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lv4t125.pdf, re-read 2026-09-29T05:08:25Z) gives tPZH, tPZL and tPHZ at 15 and 30 pF only. So the drop holds on load alone. The same point about the resistor applies to SN74LV244APWR, which this P2 did not consider.

exclusions_not_holding.part: SN74LVC1G06DBVR (C840103) and 74LVC1G06GV,125 (C12510), Texas Instruments and Nexperia, dropped under enable inverter
exclusions_not_holding.reason_given: fails delay as shown by the datasheets: the open-drain output rises through the 10 kOhm OE pull-ups (2.5 kOhm against at least 21 pF, tau 52.5 ns, 16.4 ns/V at the steepest point), slower than the 10 ns/V input transition rate the 244s allow
exclusions_not_holding.why_it_fails: The delay value is met. The rise reaches 90 % in 2.3 x 52.5 ns = 121 ns. Adding the 244's tdis, which is under 20 ns, the total is far inside the 1 us disable budget of Monostable.md:112. What the figures violate is the input transition rate of the part the inverter drives. That value is not on P2's list for this function. It also does not hold for both 244s. Nexperia 74LVC244A Rev. 14, 29 November 2024 (https://assets.nexperia.com/documents/data-sheet/74LVC_LVCH244A.pdf, read 2026-09-29T05:09:02Z) gives dt/dV 10 ns/V max at VCC 2.7 to 3.6 V. TI SCAS414AG (revised June 2026, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/sn74lvc244a.pdf, read 05:05:27Z) has no dt/dV row in its section 5.3, although its application section refers to one. The drop can stand only if the re-rank adds the driven OE pin's transition rate, from Nexperia's figure for the rank-2 alternate, as a requirement value.
